name: Local network access
plain: Asks to talk to devices on the home or office network.
meaning: Lets apps discover printers, TVs and smart-home devices and also map every device on the network. iOS has prompted since 14; Android adds it in 17.

android.permission: ACCESS_LOCAL_NETWORK (Nearby devices group); Android 16 compat flag RESTRICT_LOCAL_NETWORK
android.prompt_ui: Nearby devices prompt; system pickers can skip it
android.api_surface: Sockets to RFC 1918, 169.254/16, 100.64/10, multicast, broadcast, IPv6 link-local ranges
android.note: Apps targeting 37 must request it. Android 16 offers an opt-in compat flag with NEARBY_WIFI_DEVICES as the interim grant. DNS on port 53 and the Output Switcher are exempt.

ios.store_policy: App Review 5.1.1; Multicast Networking entitlement for raw multicast
ios.note: Denied access makes local connections fail without error.

limits.headline: Can talk to devices on your home or office network, after you tap Allow
limits.user_action: You tap Allow when the app asks to find devices on your local network
can: Find smart TVs, printers and speakers on your network
Send data to local addresses and multicast groups
Browse for devices with Bonjour on iPhone
cannot: Reach local devices if you tap Don't Allow; connections fail with no error on iPhone
Skip the prompt on iPhone, or on apps built for Android 17
Reach the internet through this permission
limits.differs: Android 17 apps must ask for local network permission. iPhone has asked since iOS 14.

story.what_it_is: An app asks to talk to devices on your home or office network.

marketing.name: Local network privacy
marketing.pitch: Apple asks you before an app can find and connect to devices on your local network.

story.for_you: You see a prompt: 'App would like to find and connect to devices on your local network'. If you allow it, the app can find your TV, printer or speaker. If you say no, casting and setup may not work.
story.for_makers: Makers need this for casting, printing and smart home control. The same access could list every device in your home, which helps a tracker build a profile. That is why Apple and now Android ask first.

use_cases.example: A video app finds your TV for casting.
A music app finds your speakers and plays to them.
A home app controls lights and plugs directly over your Wi-Fi.
A console companion app finds your console on the same network to stream to the phone.
A printer app finds your printer and sends a document.
A hidden kit scans devices on your network to build a home profile.

story.android_note: Android 17 adds a local network permission for apps that target it.
story.ios_note: iPhone has prompted since iOS 14, and apps must give a reason in a text.

history.change: Local Network Protection opt-in via RESTRICT_LOCAL_NETWORK
ACCESS_LOCAL_NETWORK runtime permission mandatory for apps targeting 37
